intro.title: Build typed modal manager API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed modal manager API in TypeScript to manage pop-up windows in a web application. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's type system to create a safe, reusable system for opening and closing modals. The core concepts involve defining custom types, using generics for flexibility, and structuring a class-based API. By the end, you'll have a fully typed manager that prevents common errors and improves code maintainability.
intro.usecase: A typed modal manager API is essential in modern web applications like admin dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and SaaS tools, where users frequently interact with modals for actions such as editing profiles, confirming purchases, or configuring settings. For example, in a project management app like Asana or Trello, developers use this pattern to manage task-creation modals, attachment previews, and team invitation dialogs with strict type safety. This ensures that each modal receives the correct props—like a task title or user ID—preventing runtime errors and improving developer experience when adding new modal types across large codebases.
